name: AI Regulatory Environment — China
blurb: Expected AI compliance burden, launch-gate delay and compute access under China's CAC-centred regime, Oct 2026.
mechanism:
China regulates AI ex ante and centrally. Public-facing generative AI must complete CAC filing — security self-assessment, test-question banks, keyword filtering, refusal-rate checks — before launch (1,112 services filed by Aug 2026), and all AI-generated content carries mandatory explicit and implicit labels (Labeling Measures + GB 45438-2025, Sept 2025). Use-specific duties come from the algorithm-recommendation provisions, the July 2026 anthropomorphic-interaction measures and PIPL; data from PIPL/DSL/the 2025 network-data regulations and the 2026 Cybersecurity Law amendment. Frontier-risk governance is soft law (AI Safety Governance Framework 2.0). There is no comprehensive AI Law yet.

Two things dominate. First, the gate: launch delay, not compliance spend, is the largest cost — ~2.8 expected months, worth ≈ 12% of a product-year at the assumed 0.5/yr obsolescence. That leaf is the model's most sensitive assumption. Second, compute: domestic accelerators cover ~55% of demand; the US now licenses H200-class exports case-by-case, but Beijing blocks them at customs, so compute_access ≈ 0.67. The import-thaw scenario shows ~56% of the gap closing when only Beijing's realisation rate moves — much of China's compute gap is self-imposed industrial policy.

Baseline: gross burden ≈ 15.8%, net ≈ 11.8% after state support; contested share ≈ 19% — higher expected cost than the US, but far more of it settled and priceable.

components.name: Shared regulatory-burden graph
components.role: One closed-form graph for every jurisdiction; a jurisdiction is a leaf binding, never a different equation set.

components.name: Instrument catalogue
components.role: Every law, regulation, standard and executive action the slots aggregate, with status, effective date, source and catalogue confidence.

components.name: China bindings
components.role: Baseline plus counterfactual scenario bindings; each leaf carries its basis inline.

inputs.name: params
inputs.description: China instrument slots (coverage, cost_share, p_in_force, p_enforced), fragmentation, ex-ante gate, state support, compute supply.

inputs.name: instrument catalogue
inputs.description: instruments.json — the sourced instrument list each slot aggregates.

outputs.name: burden_<slot>
outputs.description: Expected annual compliance cost per instrument slot, as a share of in-scope AI revenue: coverage × cost_share × p_in_force × p_enforced.

outputs.name: gross_burden / net_burden
outputs.description: variable + fixed (patchwork) + ex-ante delay burden; net subtracts state support. Shares of the reference firm's annual AI revenue.

outputs.name: gate_delay_effective_months
outputs.description: Expected launch delay imposed by ex-ante filing/approval, weighted by the gate's coverage and enforcement.

outputs.name: contested_share
outputs.description: Share of the regulatory cost at stake whose legal status is contested (4·p·(1−p) weighting: 1 at a coin flip, 0 when settled). The uncertainty a firm cannot price.

outputs.name: enforcement_gap
outputs.description: Share of in-force obligations that are not enforced in expectation — law on the books an operator can currently underweight.

outputs.name: compute_access / compute_gap
outputs.description: min(1, domestic + licensed × realised + grey) frontier-compute supply against demand. A binding min, not a smooth surrogate.

parameters.description: Pure analytical expectation over instrument slots; no simulation.
Every leaf is a sourced judgement, not a fit. Advisory until graded against filing-time and compliance-cost actuals.
Every ~60 days, aligned with CAC filing batches.

depends_on.note: Same equations.json; outputs are commensurable by construction.
China's licensed_import_ratio is set by US BIS policy; a change to the US trade slot is a rebinding here.
Jurisdiction anchor: this model is the AI regulatory environment of the China node in the 10B country tree.
The China governance cell is the 10B needs-category this regime sits under; the link is declared here because global/10B is generated and must not be hand-edited.
